en.h1: Ask your house what really happened.
en.lead: xomtra keeps years of your Home Assistant history, finds patterns and anomalies, and lets Claude or any MCP client answer questions about your home. It never changes anything in Home Assistant and runs on your own hardware.
en.note: Apache 2.0 · no account needed · data stays at home
en.q: Why did the heat pump use more energy in October than last year?
en.a: October used 412 kWh vs 349 kWh (+18 %). Most of the difference follows outside temperature (r = 0.71, 2 h lag). On 9 days the defrost cycle ran twice as often as usual, starting after the firmware update on 14 Oct.
en.f_h: What xomtra adds to Home Assistant
en.f_s: Home Assistant shows you the present. xomtra turns its history into answers.
feats: States and statistics kept for months or years in compressed Parquet files, without loading the Home Assistant database.
Entity catalog, data quality checks, correlations between devices and anomalies, ready before you ask.
xomtra only reads data and never changes anything in Home Assistant. The AI assistant gets no access to controlling your home. Roles for family members, and every query is logged.
qs: Which devices use power at night when nobody is home?
Has the bedroom humidity changed since we got the new windows?
How much did the solar panels cover of last month's consumption?
Which sensors stopped reporting this week?

faq: How much does it cost?

Nothing. xomtra is free and open source (Apache 2.0): no subscription, no account, no limits. You only use what you already have: the machine it runs on (your Home Assistant host or a small virtual machine) and, to ask in plain language, your own AI subscription, such as Claude.
Do I need Claude?
No. xomtra works with Claude Desktop, Claude.ai and any client that speaks MCP. Your AI subscription is your own; xomtra never pays or sees it.
Does my data leave the house?
Only the answers your AI client asks for, under your account. xomtra itself sends nothing anywhere unless you turn on anonymous install counting.
Can xomtra or the AI control my home?

No. xomtra only reads states, history and statistics from Home Assistant and never calls its services. Your AI assistant talks only to xomtra and gets read-only tools over xomtra's own copy of the data, never direct access to Home Assistant. Home Assistant itself has no read-only tokens, so this is guaranteed by xomtra's open source code, not by Home Assistant. With Docker, sign xomtra in as a separate Home Assistant user without admin rights, so you can revoke its access any time.
How much disk does it need?
A typical home needs 2–5 GB for 90 days of states and 5 years of hourly statistics. Large setups with years of states should use the Proxmox or VMware appliance.
Is it affiliated with Home Assistant?
No. xomtra is an independent open source project built for Home Assistant.
en.foot: xomtra is an independent open source project, not affiliated with Anthropic, the Open Home Foundation or Nabu Casa. Claude and Home Assistant are trademarks of their owners.

faq: Ile to kosztuje?

Nic. xomtra jest darmowa i open source (Apache 2.0): bez subskrypcji, bez konta, bez limitów. Korzystasz tylko z tego, co już masz: komputera, na którym działa (Twój host Home Assistant albo mała maszyna wirtualna), i do pytań zwykłym językiem z własnej subskrypcji AI, na przykład Claude.
Czy potrzebuję Claude?
Nie. xomtra działa z Claude Desktop, Claude.ai i każdym klientem MCP. Subskrypcja AI jest Twoja, xomtra za nią nie płaci i jej nie widzi.
Czy moje dane opuszczają dom?
Tylko odpowiedzi, o które prosi Twój klient AI w ramach Twojego konta. Sama xomtra niczego nie wysyła, chyba że włączysz anonimowe liczenie instalacji.
Czy xomtra albo AI może sterować moim domem?

Nie. xomtra tylko czyta z Home Assistanta stany, historię i statystyki i nigdy nie wywołuje jego usług. Asystent AI rozmawia tylko z xomtrą i dostaje wyłącznie narzędzia do odczytu własnej kopii danych xomtry, nigdy bezpośredni dostęp do Home Assistanta. Sam Home Assistant nie ma tokenów tylko do odczytu, więc gwarantuje to otwarty kod xomtry, a nie Home Assistant. W Dockerze zaloguj xomtrę jako osobnego użytkownika Home Assistanta bez uprawnień administratora, aby w każdej chwili móc odebrać jej dostęp.
Ile miejsca na dysku potrzebuje?
Typowy dom potrzebuje 2–5 GB na 90 dni stanów i 5 lat statystyk godzinowych. Duże instalacje z wieloletnią historią stanów powinny użyć appliance dla Proxmox lub VMware.
Czy to część Home Assistanta?
Nie. xomtra to niezależny projekt open source dla Home Assistanta.
pl.foot: xomtra to niezależny projekt open source, niezwiązany z Anthropic, Open Home Foundation ani Nabu Casa. Claude i Home Assistant są znakami towarowymi ich właścicieli.
